what_its_for: This medication combines two medicines in one tablet to help lower your blood pressure. Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor that relaxes your blood vessels, and hydrochlorothiazide is a water pill (diuretic) that helps your body remove extra fluid and salt. Together, they make it easier for your heart to pump blood and help keep your blood pressure at a healthy level, which lowers your risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_to_take: Take this tablet by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day so you do not forget. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Because the water pill in this medication may make you urinate more often, it is best to take it in the morning so it does not disturb your sleep at night. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your blood pressure and how well your body responds to the medication. The most common starting dose is one tablet containing lisinopril 10 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose over time if needed. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed and do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next regularly scheduled dose. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can cause your blood pressure to drop too low and make you feel dizzy or faint.
storage: Store this medication at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom, as the humidity can damage the tablets. Keep the medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of any leftover tablets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as they can raise your potassium levels to a dangerous level when combined with lisinopril. Limit alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and increase dizziness. Avoid getting too hot or becoming dehydrated — drink plenty of fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Be careful when standing up quickly, as this medicine can cause dizziness when you first stand. Avoid taking anti-inflammatory pain relievers like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve) regularly, as they can reduce how well this medication works and may harm your kidneys. Always check with your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new over-the-counter or prescription medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this could be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); difficulty breathing or swallowing; severe dizziness or fainting; little or no urination; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, slow or irregular heartbeat; or signs of low sodium such as headache, confusion, or weakness. Also call your doctor if you notice: a dry, persistent cough that does not go away (a common side effect of lisinopril); skin rash or yellowing of the skin or eyes; unusual muscle cramps or weakness; increased thirst or dry mouth; or if your blood pressure readings at home seem too high or too low.
when_it_works: You may start to see some blood pressure lowering effect within a few hours of your first dose, but it usually takes 2 to 4 weeks of taking this medication every day to get the full benefit. It is very important to keep taking this medicine even if you feel fine, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Do not stop taking it on your own — always talk to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: This medication may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Older adults (65 and older): You may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of this medication and may have a higher risk of dizziness and falls. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor you more closely. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor needs to know if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medication may not be right for you. Diabetes: This medication can affect your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar closely and let your doctor know if your readings change.
